title: Fang Bo comes from a game down to win his first WTT Star Contender Muscat qualifier a day after his Istanbul title
seo_title: WTT Star Contender Muscat: Fang Bo wins first qualifier
description: Fang Bo beat Abdullah Yigenler 3-1 on day one of WTT Star Contender Muscat qualifying, as Yang Huize, Wei Jingming and Feng Yixuan reached the main draw.
standfirst: The 34-year-old lost the opening game to Turkey's Abdullah Yigenler and then took the next three, while three Chinese teenagers came through the only round of women's qualifying.

body: Fang Bo started his second tournament in two days with a win on Monday, coming from a game down to beat Turkey's Abdullah Yigenler 9-11, 11-6, 11-8, 11-9 in the first qualifying round of WTT Star Contender Muscat.

The 34-year-old, playing for Kazakhstan, had won [WTT Contender Istanbul](/news/wtt-contender-istanbul-2026-finals-fang-bo-honoka-hashimoto-titles.html) on Sunday, his first international singles title since 2013, and travelled straight on to Oman. His match, one of the last of the day at the Sultan Qaboos Sport Complex, lasted 40 minutes.

Fang raced into an early lead in the opening game but lost it 11-9, and by Chinese accounts of the match he looked weary in the first two games. He settled after that. He led 10-6 in the third and needed a third game point to close it out. In the fourth he trailed 8-7, won three points in a row for two match points and took the second.

Fang is now the world No 66 after [climbing 94 places](/news/world-rankings-week-47-2026-fang-bo-top-100-istanbul-title.html) in Monday's ranking, and Yigenler, 27, is ranked 162nd. Fang's courtside coach in Istanbul, Li Liangfu, has said Fang played that event with a neck injury; there was no sign of a problem on Monday beyond the slow start.
## Chinese teenagers reach the women's main draw

The women's singles has only one round of qualifying in Muscat, and three Chinese teenagers came through it. Yang Huize, 16, beat Germany's Yuan Wan 11-7, 12-10, 11-7 in 22 minutes. Wei Jingming, a 17-year-old defender, beat Romania's Adina Diaconu 3-0, and Feng Yixuan, 18 and ranked 273rd, beat France's Isa Cok, the world No 150, 3-1.

Xu Yi was the Chinese player to miss out. The 21-year-old lost 3-1 to Sweden's Filippa Bergand, the top seed in qualifying and the world No 122. Kazakhstan's Sarvinoz Mirkadirova beat Claire Picard of France 3-0, Spain's Sofia-Xuan Zhang beat India's Swastika Ghosh 3-1, and Slovenia's Ana Tofant came from 2-1 down to beat Australia's Jiamuwa Wu, taking the decider 11-9 after winning a first game that went to 16-14.

China had five men in Monday's first round and lost two of them. Italy's Niagol Stoyanov, who is 39, beat 18-year-old Zhai Jiale 11-8, 11-4, 7-11, 9-11, 11-9 in 53 minutes, the longest match of the day, after Zhai had pulled level from two games down. South Korea's Lim Yunoh came from 2-1 down to beat Quan Kaiyuan, taking the decider 11-2.

Tang Yiren, 17, was taken the distance by Russia's Lev Katsman, who came back from two games down before Tang won the decider 11-9. The defender Sun Yang, 18, lost the first game to Turkey's Ibrahim Gunduz and then won three in a row, the last 14-12, and Ao Hualei beat Iran's Hamid Shams 3-1.

- Men's singles, qualifying round one: Fang Bo (KAZ) bt Abdullah Yigenler (TUR) 9-11, 11-6, 11-8, 11-9; Niagol Stoyanov (ITA) bt Zhai Jiale (CHN) 11-8, 11-4, 7-11, 9-11, 11-9; Lim Yunoh (KOR) bt Quan Kaiyuan (CHN) 11-4, 5-11, 8-11, 11-7, 11-2; Tang Yiren (CHN) bt Lev Katsman (RUS) 11-4, 13-11, 11-13, 5-11, 11-9; Sun Yang (CHN) bt Ibrahim Gunduz (TUR) 6-11, 11-5, 11-6, 14-12; Ao Hualei (CHN) bt Hamid Shams (IRI) 11-3, 13-11, 9-11, 12-10; Borgar Haug (NOR) bt Arash Shahianbidgoli (IRI) 11-1, 11-7, 6-11, 11-5; Denis Ivonin (RUS) bt Fanbo Meng (GER) 12-10, 11-6, 5-11, 11-7; Ibrahima Diaw (DEN) bt Temirlan Jiyenbayev (KAZ) 14-12, 11-5, 11-4; Maksim Grebnev (RUS) bt Bilal Al Rashdi (OMA) 11-2, 11-5, 11-5; Iskender Kharki (KAZ) bt Muhannad Al Balushi (OMA) 13-11, 11-9, 12-10; Amir Hossein Hodaei (IRI) bt Muizz Adegoke (NGR) 9-11, 11-4, 11-4, 11-8; Ebrahim Gubran (YEM) bt Abdulrahaman Abdullahi (NGR) 11-8, 8-11, 11-6, 11-7
- Women's singles, qualifying (winners reach the main draw): Yang Huize (CHN) bt Yuan Wan (GER) 11-7, 12-10, 11-7; Wei Jingming (CHN) bt Adina Diaconu (ROU) 11-9, 11-8, 11-3; Feng Yixuan (CHN) bt Isa Cok (FRA) 11-5, 9-11, 11-4, 11-6; Filippa Bergand (SWE) bt Xu Yi (CHN) 11-9, 11-9, 8-11, 11-7; Sarvinoz Mirkadirova (KAZ) bt Claire Picard (FRA) 11-9, 12-10, 11-6; Sofia-Xuan Zhang (ESP) bt Swastika Ghosh (IND) 12-10, 11-6, 7-11, 14-12; Ana Tofant (SLO) bt Jiamuwa Wu (AUS) 16-14, 4-11, 7-11, 11-8, 11-9

The men need two more wins on Tuesday to reach the main draw, which starts on Wednesday. Fang plays Romania's Eduard Ionescu, the world No 81 and third seed in qualifying, at about 8.10am UK time in the second round. Tang Yiren meets Japan's Jo Yokotani at about 9.20am, and Lim Yunoh plays Yuta Tanaka of Japan at about 9.55am, when Kang Dongsoo, whom Fang beat in the Istanbul final, also plays China's Zhou Jinquan. The final qualifying round follows from about 1pm UK time. Times are approximate.

For Germany's Dang Qiu, who goes straight into the main draw as the third seed behind Darko Jorgic and Shunsuke Togami, Muscat is the last chance to make sure of a place at the WTT Finals in Hong Kong next month: he is 13th in the race for the 16 places. Follow every match on [Eleven's event page](/events/wtt-star-contender-muscat-2026.html#matches).
